dataset.citation: Egorov et al. (2025), Gaze into the Heart, doi:10.1145/3746027.3758255

scope: Local engineering optimization and diagnostic experiments only; no production deployment
limitations: Physical camera, installed Safari/Chrome, thermals and scientific accuracy were not validated.
CPU counters measure browser process CPU time across all threads, not GPU utilization or whole-system CPU percentage.
Canvas-based cohorts change the sign of the Chromium FPS difference; all completed runs and the failed warmup are retained.
One 15-second-warmup baseline did not collect enough neutral samples; the complete comparison used 20 seconds for both variants without changing calibration policy.
GPU experiment was run after the paired CPU cohort; no randomization of delegates or matched-frame CPU/GPU QC validation was performed.
A faster GPU experiment is not permission to change the production backend policy.

dataset.citation: Egorov et al. (2025), Gaze into the Heart, doi:10.1145/3746027.3758255

runs.renderer: Apple M1, or similar

limitations: Not a scientific accuracy validation; no calibrated gaze; no physical keyboard RT.
Common video-to-canvas-to-stream adapter adds overhead in every variant.
Native browser builds under automation, not a test of installed Safari.
Concurrent pending Worker requests demonstrate overlap, not OS CPU-core utilization.
